lessons.notes:
Why most beginners lose money

In Europe, every regulated broker must show on its website how many of its ordinary (retail) clients lose money trading CFDs such as forex and Gold. When the European regulator ESMA reviewed these numbers in 2018, they ranged from 74% to 89% of retail accounts losing money. So the useful question is not why so many people lose. It is: what do the people who survive do differently? This lesson answers that question and gives you the full map of the free course.

The biggest beginner mistake: the wrong order

Most beginners watch a strategy in some video, open an account and deposit money. That is like building the roof of a house before the foundation. They cannot calculate a pip, do not know lot size and do not understand leverage. Every professional trader knows that the real difference comes less from the strategy and more from risk management and discipline. The problem is not intelligence. It is the order.

Who this course is for

  • People who know nothing about forex.
  • People who have traded, lost money, and now want to learn the basics properly.

It is for viewers in Pakistan and India, in simple Urdu/Hindi, with English subtitles on every video and written notes on this website.

Two traders, same strategy: why risk decides who survives

Two traders use exactly the same strategy with a $1,000 account. The first risks 10% of his balance on every trade, the second only 1%. Both get five losses in a row, which can happen to any strategy.

Trade10% trader: lossBalance1% trader: lossBalance

Loss 2−$90.00$810.00−$9.90$980.10

The first account is down 41% and now needs a 69% profit just to get back to $1,000. The second is down only about 5% and needs about 5%. Same strategy, completely different result. That is the answer to the opening question: the people who survive learn in the right order and control their risk on every trade. Module 8 shows how to find the right lot size from your stop loss, and you can try it now with the free lot size calculator.

How to use this course: 4 rules

  1. Watch the lessons in order. Each lesson builds on the one before.
  2. Read the notes. The notes for every lesson are free on qaziforextips.com. Read them after the video.
  3. Do the 10-minute practical task. Trading is learned by doing, not by watching.
  4. No real money until the basics are complete. First learn, then demo, then small money.

What this course is not

You will not get signals here, there is no promise of guaranteed profit, and we do not promote any broker. Forex laws are different in every country, so check your own country's rules (see forex trading in Pakistan and India). Anyone who promises a fixed daily profit is the biggest red flag (read the truth about signal groups).

How long does it take to learn forex?

There is no single answer, because everyone learns at a different speed. Some people understand the basics in two weeks, others take two months, and both are fine. One rule: move to the next lesson only when the previous lesson's idea is clear and its practical task is done. New lessons are added every day. After the basics, the next step is the free Price Action Mastery course.

Today's practical task (10 minutes)

Take a notebook and write three things:

  1. Why do I want to learn forex?
  2. How much time can I give every day?
  3. What is the most money I could lose without it affecting my life?

Answer honestly, and never put household money, loans or borrowed money at risk. Then look through the complete syllabus and start Lesson 1.1: What is forex trading?

faq: How do I start forex trading as a complete beginner?

Learn in order: first what forex is, then the trading maths (pip, lot size, spread), leverage and margin, then the platform and charts, and above all risk management. Practise on a demo account with a written plan, and only then think about a small real account. This free course follows exactly that order.
Is this forex trading course really free?
Yes. All 116 lessons are free on YouTube, with free written notes on qaziforextips.com. There is no paid upgrade inside the course.
How long does it take to learn forex trading?

Everyone learns at a different speed. Some people understand the basics in two weeks, others in two months. Move to the next lesson only when the previous idea is clear and its practical task is done.
Why do most forex traders lose money?

When the European regulator ESMA reviewed broker data in 2018, 74% to 89% of retail CFD accounts were losing money. The common reasons are learning in the wrong order, risking too much per trade and trading without a plan.
Why is risk per trade so important?

With the same strategy and five losses in a row, a trader risking 10% per trade is down about 41% and needs about 69% to recover, while a trader risking 1% is down about 5%. Small risk keeps you in the game long enough to learn.
Do you give signals or recommend a broker?
No. This course teaches how forex works and how to manage risk. It gives no signals, promises no profit and does not promote any broker.
Is the course in Urdu or Hindi?
The videos are in simple Urdu/Hindi with English trading words and English subtitles, so viewers in Pakistan and India can both follow them. The notes are in English with a Roman Urdu summary.

lessons.notes:
What is forex?

Forex comes from two English words: foreign and exchange. It means changing the currency of one country into the currency of another. When someone in Pakistan buys US dollars, when a company in India buys euros to import a machine from Europe, or when a tourist changes money into dirhams in Dubai, that is forex.

Forex trading means buying or selling a currency with the aim of profiting from a change in its price.

How big is the forex market?

According to the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Triennial Survey, about $9.6 trillion worth of currencies changed hands every day in April 2025. That is why forex is called the largest financial market in the world. It has no single building: banks and institutions around the world are linked by computers, and the market runs 24 hours a day, five days a week (see the market timings in Pakistan and India).

A simple example: the money changer

Ahmed buys 100 US dollars from a money changer at Rs 280 per dollar and pays Rs 28,000. A few days later the dollar rises to Rs 285. He sells the same 100 dollars and receives Rs 28,500: a profit of Rs 500.

If the dollar had fallen to Rs 276, he would have received Rs 27,600: a loss of Rs 400. This is the whole idea behind forex trading: profit or loss from the difference in price. (The numbers are only an example.)

Rate100 USD in rupeesResult
BuyRs 280Rs 28,000-
Sell if the dollar risesRs 285Rs 28,500+Rs 500
Sell if the dollar fallsRs 276Rs 27,600-Rs 400

Why do currency prices change?

Because of demand and supply. When many people and companies want dollars and there are few dollars available, the dollar becomes expensive. When there are plenty of dollars and few buyers, it becomes cheaper. Demand is moved by interest rates, inflation, economic news and world events. Each of these gets its own lesson later in the series.

How online forex trading works

Today most forex trading happens online. You do not hold the dollars in your hand: through a broker, on a platform such as MT5 on your computer or phone, you trade on the price going up or down.

  • Currencies are always quoted in pairs, for example the euro against the US dollar, written EUR/USD.
  • If EUR/USD rises from 1.1000 to 1.1050, the euro has become stronger against the dollar.
  • Not only currencies: Gold is traded too, as XAU/USD.
  • Pips, lots and spread come in the next lessons.

The honest truth about risk

Forex is not a job and not a get-rich-quick scheme. Price differences make losses just as easily as profits. Many regulated brokers state on their own websites that most of their retail clients' accounts lose money. The usual reason is trading without learning, without a plan and with too much risk. Anyone who promises "guaranteed profit" or "fixed daily income" is showing the biggest red flag (read about signal scams).

Is forex trading legal?

The rules are different in every country. In India, for example, the Reserve Bank of India allows residents to trade forex only through authorised persons and on recognised exchanges, for permitted purposes. Before you start anything, check the official rules of your own country. Our guide to forex trading in Pakistan and India explains the details.

The most common beginner mistake

Watching two videos, or taking someone's signal, and putting real money in on the first day. The right path is: learn first, practise on a demo account, make your own plan, then start small. This whole series follows that path.

Practical task (10 minutes)

  1. Note today's US dollar rate in rupees from a bank's website. Check it again after three days and write down who gained from the change: the person who bought dollars or the person who sold them?
  2. Write one line: "Why do I want to learn forex?" Share your answer in the YouTube comments.

faq: What is forex trading in simple words?
Forex trading is buying or selling one currency against another to profit from a change in its price, for example buying US dollars at Rs 280 and selling them at Rs 285.
How does the forex market work?
Banks, companies, institutions and individual traders exchange currencies through a worldwide computer network, 24 hours a day, five days a week. Prices move with demand and supply.
How big is the forex market?
According to the BIS Triennial Survey, average daily forex turnover was about $9.6 trillion in April 2025, which makes it the largest financial market in the world.
Can you lose money in forex trading?
Yes. The same price change that gives one trader a profit gives another a loss. Many regulated brokers state that most of their retail clients lose money. Learn first and practise on a demo account.
Is forex trading legal in Pakistan and India?

The rules depend on the country. In India the RBI allows residents to trade forex only through authorised persons and recognised exchanges for permitted purposes. Always check your own country's official rules.
How do I start forex trading as a beginner?
Learn the basics in order (this free series), open a demo account, practise with a written plan and small risk, and only then think about a small real account.
